title: Pink Tax

intro: Good morning, respected assessors. I would like to talk about a hidden cost called the Pink Tax. It is the extra price people pay for goods that are marketed to women. It sounds simple but shows deep bias in our society.

First noticed in cosmetic aisles and hair salons, the Pink Tax has grown after consumers saw patterns of higher prices for pink packaging and scented variants. It has moved from curiosity to a conversation about gender equality and ethical buying.
body: The Pink Tax shows up all around us. It is seen in toiletries, laundry detergent, toothpaste, clothing, gym memberships, when a product is marked as for girls or women. The price difference is not always due to extra ingredients. Businesses claim that design, color, or scent adds value. Yet the core product is often the same, and the only change is the packaging. In India, many women pay a premium for cosmetics that have pink wrappers and fonts, even though the formula is identical.

Some argue that cost difference is marketing. The extra colour, fragrance, or packaging is seen as a premium. Others see it as a subtle form of discrimination that pushes gendered expectations. Many companies do not openly adjust prices, but some retailers now offer the same product in a neutral box at a lower rate. If we as consumers request the unbranded version or choose the neutral option, we can pressure businesses to price fairly.

Practical action begins with awareness. Mornings at military training, we can ask young recruits to notice the label and ask their parents for the same product in a plain container. Education funds can buy generic items and display price comparison. When everyone sees that identical materials cost the same, the demand for a gendered price split will weaken. Small changes in purchasing habits, when multiplied across households, make the market feel the pull of equality.
conclusion: To sum it up, the Pink Tax is not a small inconvenience – it is a sign of deep bias that costs many more. It will slowly see change as more citizens notice the difference and ask for equal prices. Though it is easy to ignore, each small purchase can drive a big shift. I firmly believe that fairness can start with us telling brands to drop the extra mark on their female products.
Together, we can erase the Pink Tax and bring fairness to all.

opening: Every time a woman sees a pink bottle, she pays more than a man does.
closing: Together, we can erase the Pink Tax and bring fairness to all.

title: India–Russia Relations

intro: Good morning, sir. Today I will share my perspective on India‑Russia relations, a partnership that has deepened over decades and spans defence, science, and culture. It shows how two great nations can cooperate for mutual growth.

Both countries share common values of sovereignty, equality, and respect for territorial integrity. Their ties provide a strategic balance that strengthens regional stability and offers a platform for exchanging ideas in technology, renewable energy, and academic collaboration.
body: Presently, India and Russia engage in joint military exercises, sharing air defence systems and naval technology. These drills build confidence and allow both armies to learn new tactics. Simultaneously, the defence industry collaborates on converting civilian technology into weapons that meet modern battlefield needs. The partnership also involves training pilots and engineers, which improves skills and trust and fosters friendly competition leading to better preparedness.

Beyond military ties, India and Russia collaborate in science and technology. Joint research laboratories work on space missions, quantum computing, and medical breakthroughs. Both governments encourage startup ecosystems to innovate together, creating jobs and fostering a culture of shared expertise. This collaboration also reduces costs by sharing resources, and it strengthens India’s reputation as a technology hub while enhancing Russian expertise in emerging fields in depth.

On the economic front, trade volumes grow steadily. Both sides sponsor joint ventures in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture. A practical step for individual officers is to master language skills that facilitate communication with Russian counterparts, ensuring smoother exchanges and fewer misunderstandings during joint missions. This linguistic preparedness also boosts confidence, allowing officers to act decisively and maintain operational excellence when facing diverse cultural settings always.
conclusion: I believe that India‑Russia ties embody a model of partnership based on respect and shared prosperity. Continued interaction will deepen trust, strengthen defence, and broaden technological horizons for both nations. This synergy will inspire the next generation to pursue peace together.

Moving forward, we must stay vigilant about threats, avoid overreliance, and keep our initiatives based on mutual benefit. With disciplined effort, this partnership will endure and contribute to a stable, prosperous future for our nation.

opening: India and Russia together chart a path of shared strength and mutual respect.
closing: Let us move forward, knowing that our partnership will endure and lead to a safer, stronger future.

title: ASEAN

intro: Hello, I am here to talk about ASEAN. ASEAN is a group of neighbour states in South East Asia that share common values and work together on trade, security, and culture. Understanding it helps future officers.

I need to explain why this matters. ASEAN illustrates regional cooperation. For an officer who will protect borders and foster peace, knowing its values adds a useful perspective. It also shows how allies can work together.
body: As ASEAN has grown, it has created a forum where leaders discuss economic ties, people’s welfare and security threats. Members differ in size and influence, yet they try to reach agreements that respect each nation’s sovereignty. The current focus is on deepening trade links and sharing best practices on humanitarian issues. This balanced approach keeps the region stable and offers learning opportunities for a future officer.

India views ASEAN as a strategic partner that can help address regional security and economic challenges. Under a shared vision of open markets and connectivity, India has contributed resources to support development projects across these states. At the same time, Indian leaders urge for greater military engagement and intelligence sharing. For a prospective officer, understanding this partnership shows how national interests align with regional commitments.

One practical step for any officer is to foster people‑to‑people relations through exchange programs. Schools, universities and cultural groups circulate ideas, build trust and reduce misunderstandings. When soldiers or diplomats encounter friendly faces from ASEAN, the bonds strengthen. This simple act allows long‑term peace to grow, and it illustrates how cooperation can turn competition into mutual support. Such initiatives demonstrate respect for cultural diversity and signal openness to joint missions in future crises.
conclusion: It is clear that ASEAN offers lessons in unity and diversity. An officer must balance national duty with regional diplomacy, recognizing that cooperation builds security for all. The future will test these ties through shared challenges and emerging opportunities.

I believe that by embracing ASEAN’s cooperative spirit, we strengthen our nation’s response to global shifts. Let us act with empathy, respect, and resolve. Together, we can build a safer, more integrated future for all.

opening: Hello, I am here to talk about ASEAN.
closing: Together, we can build a safer, more integrated future for all.

title: India and Its Neighbours

intro: Good morning, officers. Today I will talk about India and Its Neighbours. This topic invites us to look beyond borders and think about how our country interacts with those who share the same land and cultures. In this discussion I will share the current situation, the main points of India’s relations, and a practical step we can all consider. Together we will see that cooperation is both an opportunity and a responsibility.
body: India shares borders with several neighbours, each having their own histories and concerns. Some of these across the frontier have long‑standing disputes, others maintain trade ties, while a few have minor border friction. The government speaks of a neighbourhood policy that encourages dialogue and shared prosperity. Yet, on the field, tensions can surface from crossing points, religious differences, or competition for resources. Navigating this complexity requires disciplined leadership and empathy.

India’s neighbour to the east looks to expand connectivity through shared rail and road links. The other side sees the need for security checks, especially where river basins overlap. On the western front, partnerships focus on maritime safety and sharing of water. In the south, collaboration on cultural festivals keeps communities united. Despite the mixing, each side has its own security concerns and economic aspirations, so a balanced approach is essential.

One small step you could take is to study the local languages and customs of a neighbour state before you visit. Knowledge of a simple greeting or a traditional dish can break the ice with soldiers or civilians alike. It shows respect and opens communication channels. Incorporating this habit into training improves your cultural awareness and strengthens goodwill, which are huge assets in any peace‑keeping or diplomatic mission.
conclusion: To recap, India’s relationships with its neighbours are complex but full of promise. Cooperation on trade, water sharing and cultural exchange can build a stable map. The prospects for peace grow as trust deepens. It will take continued dialogue, clear communication and mutual respect to turn prospects into reality.

But some challenges remain. Resource competition and outdated boundaries still spark doubts. Every officer must watch for misinformation and stay fair in judgement. I believe that by keeping a calm mind and honest intentions, we can transform friction into friendship. Let us move forward with courage, steady insight and a conviction that shared goals outweigh individual differences.

closing: Let us move forward with courage, steady insight and a conviction that shared goals outweigh individual differences.

title: My Role Model

intro: Good morning, sir and madam. I am here to speak about a topic that is close to my heart and helps shape my vision for the future. My role model is not a famous personality but rather a core principle that guides my actions every day. Every day, I start with a mantra that steers me toward clarity and purpose.

In choosing a role model, I consider traits that resonate with the values we cherish in service. Honesty, resilience, and compassion are the pillars I try to emulate. They aren’t about fame but about the impact one leaves on the lives around them, especially in a diverse nation that thrives on unity and shared purpose. These qualities shape my daily interactions, from handling small duties to stepping into bigger responsibilities.
body: Today, I find myself in training and in civilian life, facing daily challenges that test my patience and decision making. The model I look up to reminds me that steadiness in hard times is the key to earning the trust of peers. I also see moments when doubt creeps in, remembering that steadiness aids in holding my resolve.

This principle teaches me that leadership is less about authority and more about listening. In our ranks, listening to the concerns of subordinates fosters morale and cooperation. By putting an open ear to every voice, I can act in ways that uplift the collective mission. By reflecting on these experiences, I continually sharpen my listening skills and adapt my leadership style.

Within our diverse society, humility is a bridge between different ethnic and religious groups. When I take a step to volunteer with local communities, I practice this humility daily, learning that collective service can bind us beyond differences. Moreover, engaging in community projects opens doors to learning about traditional ways and modern challenges.
conclusion: I look forward to applying these lessons every day, the challenges will be many, but with integrity, I will navigate them.
In the end, my role model is not a distant mirror but a living practice that I refine as I grow. Let this belief guide us towards a brighter future for all.

closing: Let this belief guide us towards a brighter future for all.

title: Evolution of Telecommunication

intro: Good morning, officers, thank you for this chance to discuss a subject touching all our lives: the evolution of telecommunication.

From knocking on drums to touching screens, this field has grown into a global, mutually connection that ties us together. It shows how human need to share grows. That change is woven into everyday, daily life, allowing each of us to connect, learn, and serve our nation efficiently and continually.
body: Today, every corner of our land feels the pull of fast links. Satellites guide signals, and fiber cables stretch across plains and cities. The speed and reliability of voice, data, and video turn communication into a backbone for governance and commerce. Yet the ease that connects us asks us to keep pace with new protocols that demand efficient, secure, and adaptable networks.

Coverage, speed, affordability, and security are the main points. The gap between cities and remote villages still exists. Speed gives instant video proof and quick knowledge sharing. Cheaper links sometimes sacrifice safety and privacy. In our country, broadband rollout in rural areas has improved reach, but many still lack reliable fixed service. A practical step is to support community Wi‑Fi hubs that pool resources, extend reach, and offer safe‑usage training.

These phases will test our resilience. Satellite‑based broadband may bring faster nodes, but stronger security and reliable hand‑offs are needed. We must keep data safe while it moves. Oversight from administration and participation from local users are key. In my view, many small steps bridge a big gap: community forums, shared learning, and clear testing. Let us stay vigilant, share responsibly, and let technology grow as an ally.
conclusion: Telecommunication has shifted from simple signals to a national backbone. Speed, reach, and security now orchestrate our civic life. The challenge is to keep this network open, fair, and humane, critical for growth and society.
I trust that by building community hubs and safeguarding data, we will foster a connected nation that listens. Let technology echo in every heart, and together we nurture and drive progress.

opening: Good morning, officers, let us explore the remarkable evolution of telecommunication.
closing: Let technology echo in every heart, and together we nurture and drive progress.

title: Naxalism

intro: Good morning, officers. Today I will talk about a problem that has grown in some parts of our country – Naxalism. It is a challenge that touches both politics and the lives of ordinary people everyday.

Naxalism refers to a form of armed rebellion that seeks to overthrow the state violent means. It began decades in rural areas where poverty and marginalisation created fertile ground for the movement to take hold.
body: The threat of Naxalism remains in several states across the country. In additional remote forests and hilly regions, small insurgent groups employ guerrilla tactics, striking at police posts and transport routes. The government battles to maintain law and order while villagers often feel entangled between militants and authorities. Many families suffer fear and uncertainty that disrupts everyday life and economic stagnation that frightens many.

Those who support the movement say that prolonged neglect of infrastructure and basic needs compels people to rise. They highlight inadequate roads, lack of electricity, and limited education as catalysts. Critics argue that the use of violence ruins livelihoods, stifles trade, and erodes democratic values. They insist that a strong state must protect its citizens and ensure fairness for all, and against proposed development.

In the current Indian context, strategies emphasize a balanced approach. While security forces remain essential, communities now participate in identifying threats. Through support for local schools, healthcare centers, and livelihood projects, trust grows. Governors and army units often hold meetings with village heads, listening to grievances. This partnership not only helps prevent recruitment but also demonstrates that development can coexist with security overall.
conclusion: To summarise, Naxalism is not just a security problem but a social one. It reminds us that governance must reach every corner. The future demands a blend of vigilance and empathy, ensuring that every community feels safe and represented.

Challenges remain—long–distance monitoring, mistrust and rapid changes of leadership. I believe that collaboration, dialogue and development are weapons. Let us champion a future where safety and growth walk hand in hand.

closing: Let us champion a future where safety and growth walk hand in hand.

title: Women as Leaders

intro: Good morning, assessors. Today I speak on women as leaders, a theme that brings courage, insight, and societal progress.
For years, women have stepped into roles that demand vision and care, yet many still face bias, stereotypes, and limited access to authority.
body: In contemporary India, we see more women leading businesses, schools, and communities, yet their journey is uneven across regions and classes. Some regions celebrate female leaders openly, while in others, cultural norms still limit participation. These disparities stem from historical roles, education gaps, and sometimes deep-rooted traditions. Every gap closes when society values diverse input, leading to shared wisdom that benefits all for everyone, including future generations, in every village.

The advantage of women leaders is clear: they are often better at listening, collaboration, and crisis negotiation. These skills foster unity and stability. Critics argue they may be less decisive, but leaders who blend empathy with firmness keep teams focused. Thus, the value lies in balance, not in a single trait. This balance empowers communities, strengthens governance, and inspires future leaders to seek thoughtful, inclusive policies that reflect shared goals.

In India, community groups began inviting women into decision‑making circles, recognizing their unique perspective. A practical step for anyone is to mentor one woman with leadership traits, offering her real responsibilities, regular guidance, and public acknowledgment. When mentors and mentees collaborate, confidence rises and the culture shifts, turning individual growth into collective change. By cultivating this network, communities build resilience, adapt to change, and create lasting pathways for all women to lead confidently within society.
conclusion: As we look ahead, the rise of women leaders signals hope for sharper decision making, inclusive governance, and a more compassionate society.

We must protect their opportunities, challenge old assumptions, and ensure that every woman’s voice is heard. By valuing their insights, we strengthen the nation and honor the principle that true leadership is shared. Because when society trusts and supports each leader equally, progress becomes collective, sustainable, and rooted in justice for all members. Such a future calls for concerted effort from every citizen, especially empowering the younger generation to step forward confidently as future stewards.

opening: Good morning, assessors—women as leaders is not a trend but a transformative force shaping our future.
closing: Let us all pledge to nurture and celebrate leaders of all genders, for a society that thrives on inclusive power.

title: India–Germany Relations

intro: Good evening, officers. I am delighted to discuss India–Germany relations. It is a partnership that blends history, trade, science and cultural ties between two large and influential nations.

These ties matter because India can learn from Germany’s technology and sustainability practices, while Germany gains access to India’s growing markets and youthful talent. Both countries seek balanced growth and shared innovation. Together they aim to build a partnership that benefits people, progress and global stability.
body: Presently, India and Germany collaborate across many sectors. In science and technology, joint research focuses on renewable energy, medical breakthroughs, and digital infrastructure. Both governments have encouraged start‑ups and R&D centers, creating valuable cross‑knowledge exchange. Moreover, there have been frequent visits by business delegations that explore co‑development projects and enhance bilateral trust.

India values Germany’s expertise in engineering and environmental sustainability. Germany benefits from India’s dynamic markets and cultural diversity, which helps German firms adapt to new consumer segments. This mutual appreciation reinforces trade flows, shared standards, and joint investments in smart manufacturing. Additionally, educational exchanges have increased, with many Indian students pursuing advanced studies in German universities, bringing fresh perspectives back home. These exchanges inspire innovations that benefit both economies.

A practical step for India is to strengthen technical collaborations by setting up joint innovation labs that focus on climate solutions. These labs would bring together Indian scientists, German engineers, and industry leaders, turning research into marketable products and creating jobs for the nation. The labs could also support digital services and automotive technologies, sharing best practices and helping both sides stay competitive in a rapidly changing global market. Such collaborations reinforce confidence and build a resilient partnership that can answer tomorrow’s challenges.
conclusion: India–Germany relations have grown from diplomatic visits to deepen technology and trade ties. Our aim should be to keep this momentum alive, translating cooperation into tangible benefits for citizens of both nations.

While challenges like balancing industrial standards and navigating cultural nuances exist, we must stay focused, adaptable, and respectful. I believe that with mutual trust, we can create a partnership that propels both India and Germany toward a brighter, sustainable future.

opening: Let us explore how India and Germany are building a dynamic partnership.
closing: India and Germany together can shape a resilient future based on shared vision and mutual growth.

title: India as a Superpower

intro: Good morning, officers. Today I will talk about India as a superpower, a topic that gathers curiosity because it questions our place on the world map and what this status means for us and our country.

Understanding this idea helps us see India’s role in global affairs, its growth, and the challenges ahead. We must view it with both optimism and realistic scrutiny for all of us in shaping our future.
body: India is stepping forward on the world stage, drawing attention for its economic dynamism and strategic location. The nation now shares a voice in many regional groups and enjoys growing influence in international summits. This rise is driven by vast human resources, a youthful population and new technologies that allow us to keep pace with global trends. India’s diversified economy also supports its growing global footprint everywhere.

Yet, being a superpower also invites scrutiny. India faces internal challenges such as infrastructure gaps, regional disparities, and the need to safeguard human rights for all communities. On the international front, balancing relations with neighboring powers and adapting to shifts in global alliances test our diplomatic skill. Recognition of these weaknesses allows us to craft more resilient policies.

To build on this momentum, India can strengthen its scientific research and green technologies. Investing in clean energy projects, expanding digital infrastructure, and encouraging innovation through universities will create a self‑sustaining growth engine. This practical step reduces dependence on foreign supplies and reinforces India’s position as a reliable partner in addressing global challenges. These actions also open doors for local talent to thrive, ensuring the future workforce is skilled and ready to meet global demands.
conclusion: Looking ahead, India must keep building on its strengths and learning from its challenges. Managing internal diversity, protecting our environment, and inspiring future leaders will define our journey. Our role as a superpower is not just about power but responsibility.

I firmly believe India’s path to superpower status requires unity, innovation, and ethical governance. Staying true to these principles will unlock our full potential. Let us step forward with courage.

opening: Good morning, officers – let us explore India’s ascent toward superpower status.
closing: Let us step forward with courage and purpose.

title: Video Piracy

intro: Good morning, today I will discuss video piracy in sports and media. It means illegally sharing or downloading athletic events and film content for free. This practice has grown with the internet, affecting both fans and creators. It raises key questions about ownership, fairness, and the future of fan engagement.
Video piracy began when home video tapes became cheap, then spread with file sharing sites. Over time, the motive was simple: fans could view games they could not attend.
body: Today, the situation looks complex. Some fans feel a right to watch their favourite sport without cost. Broadcasters and teams rely on ticket sales and ads for revenue. Without permission, organisers lose a vital income that funds better facilities, training and player pay. Hidden growth becomes hard to keep and the digital divide.

There are two views. Some say sports video is a public good that should spread freely, sharing culture. Others insist that streaming without a licence breaks legal rules. Without revenue, sponsors lose confidence, and athletes see less payoff. A compromise is to offer affordable official streams that let fans support the sport responsibly in the long term.

In India, mobile internet makes piracy easy. Many fans want to watch cricket or football from local clubs, and illegal downloads give instant fixes. Yet laws protect creators, and broadcasters block unauthorized sites. A practical step is to subscribe to a legal streaming service, which offers quality and supports the sport for future championships.
conclusion: Video piracy hurts the sports industry. Free access may be tempting, but it cuts revenue needed for training and facilities. The future depends on everyone working together. Transparent pricing, free learning clips, and official streams can help.

My view is that protecting creative rights keeps the sport fair for everyone. The law must be enforced, and awareness raised. Choosing official streams lets the industry grow healthy, keeping competition vibrant. Let us move forward with ethics, respect, and commitment to support all who work hard for the game.

opening: Good morning, today I will discuss video piracy in sports and media.
closing: In the end, protecting creative work ensures a vibrant future for all.

title: Artificial Intelligence

intro: I greet the board with confidence, and today I will talk about artificial intelligence. This field blends science and imagination, giving machines skills that were once purely human. It shapes our future at home and beyond.

Artificial intelligence refers to systems that learn, reason, and adapt to new data. In today's world, it is present in simple voice assistants, medical diagnostics, and autonomous vehicles, connecting people to new possibilities.
body: Today, most industries use AI for tasks that require speed and precision. In healthcare, algorithms screen scans with accuracy, while in agriculture they predict weather patterns to improve yields. Even our everyday phones learn from our habits. These developments show that AI is no longer a futuristic idea but a working reality that enhances efficiency in many sectors, in the processes of production and daily operations.

AI brings many benefits, such as faster data analysis and reduced human error. Yet it also raises concerns about privacy, job losses, and unequal access. In India, the government encourages research in smart cities and rural connectivity, while private companies are building AI in healthcare and e-commerce. A practical step for us is to develop data ethics, ensuring that AI systems respect confidentiality and fairness.

To harness AI responsibly, we should start by learning machine learning fundamentals through free online courses. This knowledge sets a solid base for understanding how algorithms work and how to spot bias. Sustained learning keeps you updated with new tools, fostering confidence in decisions. As officer cadets, you will face complex decisions where AI plays a role; a strong grasp of its limits will help you lead wisely.
conclusion: I believe AI will reshape our duties, making decisions faster but also demanding critical thinking. The challenge lies in balancing progress with safety, ensuring we protect privacy and avoid overreliance. We must be vigilant stewards of this power.

As candidates, let us embrace AI with awareness and responsibility, using it to serve the nation and its people. Our disciplined thinking will be the shield that guides prudent use of this revolutionary tool.

opening: Greetings, today I will share how artificial intelligence is reshaping our world.
closing: Let us harness AI wisely, for the benefit of ourselves and the nation.

title: India–Pakistan Relations

intro: Good morning, sir. India and Pakistan share a long and complex story that shapes matters for all of us. Understanding the ties between them helps us think clearly about peace and progress.

Both sides grew from the same land, they share music, food, and language, but different faith and politics turned friendship into tension. The border remains a sensitive spot, with occasional skirmishes pulling tensions higher.
body: Today the main issue is the border line. Unresolved matters about security equipment and troop deployment still provoke mistrust. Beyond the front, humanitarian concerns for refugees, families divided by the line, and the need for better policing methods keep both governments busy. Small skirmishes sometimes spill beyond the ring of steel, forcing both sides to keep their eyes sharp. We must keep calm eyes on dialogue.

One key point is security. Mutual understanding here can prevent accidental clashes. There are also shared cultural values: food, music, and festivals that remind people of common roots. Beyond culture, trade offers hope. If both sides open markets to one another, small businesses could grow and provide employment for many families that feel caught in the crossfire.

From India’s side, building confidence is essential. Practical steps include accepting joint patrols on disputed stretches and sharing intelligence about insurgent movements. Another step is encouraging people-to-people contacts in border villages, so that families can meet without fear. By taking these small gestures, we may slowly reduce the wall of suspicion that has grown over years. Pride in unity can keep fear away.
conclusion: In short, stability hinges on trust, dialogue and small steps. For us, it means keeping the border safer, listening to families on both sides and working for better trade and cooperation.

I believe that a calm and open mindset will ease distrust over time. Let us work together to keep peace alive, always remembering the shared heritage that connects us all. I am confident that with joint action we can turn tension into friendship.

opening: India and Pakistan share a long and complex story that shapes our nation.
closing: Let us keep the door open to peace and hope.

title: Women in Defence

intro: Good morning, officers. Today I would like to talk about women in defence, a subject that reflects our changing society and growing strength of those who serve. Women have increasingly embraced roles that were once seen as off limits.

While some still observe traditional views, many officers and institutions recognize the importance of diverse perspectives and argue that a uniform of gender parity brings fresh ideas and better decision making for our future.
body: Across the navy, army and air force, women are shifting from support posts to technical and leadership positions. This shift brings fresh viewpoints and strengthens teamwork. Yet the change is not without obstacles; unconscious bias and lack of role models still hinder progress. In India, more women are joining and serving with pride, but the number of senior posts open to them is still small.

One of the most effective ways to ease this transition is mentorship combined with targeted skill training. Senior officers can pair with younger women to share experiences, navigate career paths, and endorse them for challenging roles. Technical courses in avionics, cyber defence and logistics have shown that when women receive the same rigorous training as men, they rise to meet the demands of a modern battlefield.

Beyond training, the institute’s culture must celebrate success stories and foster an environment that says 'no excuses for bias.' Officers should be trained to spot subtle stereotypes and actively support their female peers. If we build a culture where the competence of a woman is judged by her merit, the whole defence ecosystem will thrive in all operations and strategic dilemmas and will inspire future generations.
conclusion: Putting all this together, the progress of women in defence is a win for equality and for the strength of our security forces. It requires commitment from all ranks to break old habits and to pave new paths.
I firmly believe that every woman who feels the call to serve deserves the same chances as any man. As officers, let us lead by example and create an environment where talent shines above any label.

opening: Good morning, officers, today I would like to talk about women in defence as a vital topic for our modern army.
closing: As officers, let us lead by example and create an environment where talent shines above any label.

title: Division of States in India

intro: Good morning, esteemed assessors. Today I want to talk about an important topic that shapes how India works – the division of states. It is simple in name but huge in impact, because it decides how the country is organized for governance, resource sharing and local identity.

The idea emerged after independence when the nation needed to accommodate a huge mix of languages, cultures and historic regions. Government created new states to give people voice and manage local issues better.
body: Today India consists of numerous states, many of which have their own legislative and executive bodies. When a state grows too large in terms of population, area or cultural diversity, its administration can become slow and distant. In such cases the option of creating a smaller state often appears as a solution that brings decision‑making closer to the people and can increase efficiency. Many communities feel this change will empower them. The central government monitors progress closely.

On the positive side, smaller states can respond faster to local needs, tailor development schemes and preserve cultural identity. Critics argue that too many states could lead to unnecessary competition, higher administrative costs and risk of division of resources. A balanced approach involves a clear set of criteria that looks at economic sustainability, social cohesion and clear boundaries before any new creation. Historically, such changes often arise from long‑standing grievances but must be managed carefully to prevent social friction.

To make it real, local leaders can form a joint task force that includes representatives from all affected districts, consult with citizens through forums, and draft a transparent blueprint. The committee should also draft a timetable to monitor progress and hold the newly formed state accountable. Public transparency is key to maintaining trust through such transitions. The model should include mechanisms for equitable revenue sharing, to ensure new states have the capacity to meet public needs.
conclusion: In summary, dividing states is not just a line on a map; it is a tool for bringing governance closer to the people, respecting cultural identities and improving administrative efficiency. Yet it also brings fresh challenges in resource sharing, potential conflicts and costs.

I believe that balanced approach, guided by consensus and rationality, will ensure that state formation strengthens democracy. As India grows, we must keep unity while giving space for voices; careful planning is the key to lasting harmony.

opening: Let us explore how the division of states shapes India’s past, present and future.
closing: By balancing unity with autonomy, we can build a stronger, more inclusive India for generations.
